intelligence.essence: Nothing counts as landed until it is on his screen, in place, working — the gate behind the pedestal, the library, the agreement page, and the language itself. His eye is the final compile, the day's teaching must be countable, and the words he already gave are build instructions, not questions to re-ask.
intelligence.human_view: You stop hearing 'it's ready' and start seeing finished things: the library where you can open it, the formats placed where they belong, the agreement page looking and feeling the way the best page already does. And each day's lessons get counted — the ten smartest and the ten most valuable — so progress is something you can point at.
intelligence.child_view: Saying 'I built it' isn't the same as showing it standing in the room. We bring the finished thing and put it where you can see it and touch it. That's when it counts.
intelligence.grandma_view: He likes a thing, he describes a thing, and then weeks later discovers it was never actually placed where he could use it. So the rule became simple: it isn't done until he's looking at it, working, on his own screen. His earlier words count too — when he's already told us, we build it instead of asking again.
intelligence.ai_view: Operating rules distilled from SN-3225..SN-3234: (1) The Pedestal: nothing flat, everything a real object — sidebar icons take the sharp bottom-bar circle form, harvested verbatim; the bottom bar is the reference object for icons. (2) The Library gate: 'I have to see it' — liking the unfold, the slideshow, and the Library is not having them; a thing is landed only when he sees it on his screen, in place, working. (3) Format assignment: unfold in About, slideshow in Skills, Personal done; fast action is the mode — action done right away, with quality — not mere speed. (4) The performance question: the day's teaching must be countable — top ten intelligent + top ten most valuable, every day, named; the count is the proof. (5) The language I live in: official, forevermore — the eight documents are not a reference but the place the work lives: speak in it, design in it, operate in it. (6) The agreement page look: play button, her picture, her name — harvested from the free walk end slide that already looks right. (7) The agreement page feel: orb, geo corners, sharp and real — feel is first, not polish at the end. (8) The two choices: listen-and-read or a visual slideshow — the choice itself is the showcase. (9) The font: Marcellus, found — type is the face of the page; losing it lost the layering. (10) The vault rule: nothing made yesterday and gone — everything made goes in the vault the moment it is made, live on made.
intelligence.what_it_means: Seeing is the only acceptance test that cannot be gamed by a status report: this group welds the delivery standard (in place, in front of his eye) to the input standard (his prior word is already the instruction) — the two halves of finishing.

page.machine: 1) Acceptance = seen in place, working, in a real profile — never a status claim. 2) Prior word = build instruction; never re-ask a decided question. 3) Daily teaching counted: 10 intelligent + 10 valuable, named. 4) Language: lived in (speak/design/operate), not consulted. 5) Every made asset enters the vault at creation.
page.why_it_matters: This is the Readiness Standard in its original form, dictated a week before it got its name: prepared is not ready, described is not delivered. Every gate Resolve has hardened since runs on this group's rule.
page.how_it_connects: Sixth movement of batch 14. It states the acceptance gate that SN-4740's page-to-ten procedure must pass, and it is the same standard this batch's own proofs follow — every claim in the batch records is read back from landed bytes, not asserted.
page.what_is_in_it_for_you: You get shown, not told: finished things in front of your eyes, your earlier decisions honored without being re-asked, and a daily count that proves the team is actually learning.
page.the_learning: From now on, work closes when it is seen working in place — and a word already given is executed, never re-asked — instead of a completion claim standing in for the sight of the thing.
